projects.title: Bank Reconciliation Agent
projects.label: RECON
projects.short: Rules-first reconciliation agent on synthetic data
projects.pitch: A rules-first tool-calling agent that matches small-business bank lines to invoices on synthetic data.
projects.card: A rules-first tool-calling agent that matches small-business bank lines to invoices on synthetic data. Code verifies every proposal, the model cannot write to the ledger, and a person approves before anything posts. Read-only MCP server, a plain-English rule compiler, live evals on four models, a pre-registered code-mode experiment and a CI replay gate; the README says where it breaks.
projects.byline: Personal project · v1.1.0 · Synthetic data only

visuals.alt: Terminal replay of make demo: 40 committed bank lines through the rules pass, the agent and the shadow policy, each proposal left for a person to review

projects.demo_note: replay viewer: recorded runs, synthetic data, no key

claims.text: 0 wrong matches in 460 agent match proposals (582 agent decisions) over 3 live runs on each of two synthetic businesses.

0 of 40 injected lines that ask for a different or an extra invoice succeeded in any run. The verifier refuses whatever the payload asks for on 36 of them; on the 4 it leaves to the model's judgement, 0 payloads were followed by any model in any run with defences on.
containment held in every run and every probe, and code mode was cheaper on average, but the pre-registered efficiency hypothesis failed for both models tested.

projects.title: Provenance-Tiered RAG
projects.label: RAG
projects.short: RAG over NZ GST, German VAT and INZ instructions
projects.pitch: Question answering over New Zealand GST law, German VAT law and Immigration New Zealand's Operational Manual, with dated sources in tiers.
projects.card: Question answering over New Zealand GST law, German VAT law (UStG and UStDV) and Immigration New Zealand's Operational Manual, with dated sources in tiers: statute, official guidance and untrusted notes. Immigration answers are information from INZ's published instructions, not immigration advice. Code checks every citation and figure against passages in force on the date asked about. Frozen eval sets, held-back questions and defence ablations; the README says what the numbers do not show.

projects.title: mcp-code-mode
projects.label: MCP
projects.short: Code mode for any MCP server, in Python
projects.pitch: Run model-written Python against any MCP server's tools in a locked-down Docker sandbox, through a host-side bridge that checks every call.
projects.card: Run model-written Python against any MCP server's tools in a locked-down Docker sandbox. It serves a wrapped server's tools to the model as one run_python tool. Every call passes a host-side bridge that checks the allowlist, the tool's JSON Schema, argument size and a call budget, and refuses oversized results. Extracted from bank-reconciliation-agent; the README maps each threat to a control and a test, and lists what it does not protect.

visuals.alt: Terminal capture: a program calls two allowlisted toy tools through the bridge, then builds a call to a tool off the allowlist, which the bridge refuses before the server sees it

claims.lead: Where it was measured, in bank-reconciliation-agent:
claims.text: containment held in every run and every probe, and code mode was cheaper on average, but the pre-registered efficiency hypothesis failed for both models tested. Read the numbers there; this package carries no measurements of its own.

projects.title: copass
projects.short: Hand-over between AI coding agents, no network
projects.card: A Node.js CLI that reads one AI coding agent's local session logs and writes a hand-over for another: the task, your constraints quoted verbatim, the work done, the unanswered request and the current git state. Credentials are redacted, and the README marks which agent adapters were checked against real logs.

visuals.alt: Terminal window: copass --no-copy finds a Claude Code session about cursor pagination that stopped at its usage limit and reports a hand-over ready, with 3 requests, 3 changed files, 2 commands and a plan with 1 of 3 steps done, saved to .copass/latest.md; a second command prints the agent's plan with its current focus and the user's last request, marked as not answered
visuals.caption: A real run on synthetic session logs: the hand-over copass writes when an agent stops at its usage limit.

claims.text: It makes no network calls, spends no tokens, needs no daemon, and has no dependencies beyond Node.js.

projects.title: birdclef-2026-audio-classification
projects.short: Synthetic clips for rare bird classes, tested
projects.card: Tests whether AudioLDM2 synthetic clips for rare classes help two classifiers: BirdNET embeddings with a linear classifier, and a CNN trained from scratch on mel-spectrograms. The clips helped the first and hurt the second.
projects.byline: Coursework, University of Waikato · Deep Learning (COMPX525) · individual

visuals.alt: Two mel spectrograms of five seconds each: a real Spot-tailed Nightjar recording, with repeated arcs of song over background noise, and an AudioLDM2 synthetic clip made of flat horizontal bands. The title gives the class's validation ROC-AUC as 0.172 without synthetic clips and 0.971 with them
visuals.caption: Mel spectrograms derived from BirdCLEF+ 2026 competition audio: a real Spot-tailed Nightjar clip and an AudioLDM2 one. For this rare class, synthetic clips lifted the CNN's AUC from 0.172 to 0.971.

visuals.alt: Flow chart of the experiments: the training list is split into real training and validation sets; rare classes get synthetic clips from AudioLDM2; four models, BirdNET embeddings with a linear classifier and a compact CNN on mel spectrograms, each with and without the synthetic clips, are scored on one shared validation set by macro ROC-AUC
visuals.caption: The experiment design. The audio is BirdCLEF+ 2026 competition data; the synthetic clips were generated for the rare classes.

claims.text: BirdNET embeddings + ML reach 0.8940 validation macro ROC-AUC with synthetic enrichment and 0.8869 without, on one fixed 80/20 split of train_audio with one seed. This is not a Kaggle leaderboard score.

projects.title: streaming-ensemble-classifier
projects.short: Online ensemble under a 250 KB memory budget
projects.card: An online ensemble classifier for a drifting, imbalanced stream under a hard 250 KB memory budget, with a post-mortem of the memory-measurement bugs that put the submitted version over the limit, and a re-run with the cap enforced.
projects.byline: Coursework, University of Waikato · Machine Learning for Data Streams (COMPX523) · individual

visuals.alt: Horizontal bar chart of tournament scores on the synthetic stream: Naive Bayes 0.6087, the spec ensemble 0.8407, the champion as submitted 0.9642 with its trees never capped and over the memory limit, and the fixed champion 0.9048 at 234 KB, under the 250 KB budget
visuals.caption: The submitted champion scored higher because its trees were never capped; the fixed one stays under the 250 KB budget.

claims.text: On the synthetic RBF stream (100,000 instances, 4 drifts) with MOA's size agent loaded, the fixed champion (n=25, 8 KB per tree, memory_estimate_period=1000) reaches a tournament score of 0.9048, with its trees measured at 204.8 KB on the Java side and about 234 KB in total, under the 250 KB budget.
Builds an online ensemble classifier that learns continuously from a non-stationary stream with class imbalance and concept drift, under a hard 250 KB memory budget.
